name: Distortion Cascade
description: Gradually increase distortion/saturation on a layer over time. The sound degrades from clean to destroyed, creating tension and textural evolution.
usefulWhen: Building intensity over time, creating a sense of degradation or escalation
repair: Use parallel processing — blend clean and distorted signals. Too much distortion across all layers creates ear fatigue.
strudelHints: Layer multiple voices with increasing gain for perceived distortion
Use .gain() modulation with high values on fast subdivisions

name: Spectral Shift
description: Dramatically change the frequency content of a sound — open or close filters, emphasize different harmonics, shift the spectral center of gravity.
usefulWhen: A sound needs to evolve or transform without changing its rhythmic/melodic content
repair: The shift should happen over at least 4 cycles. Instant filter jumps are jarring unless that's the specific intent.
strudelHints: .lpf() with slow modulation '<200 2000 500 3000 200>'.slow(16)
.hpf() to remove low end for a 'thinning' effect
Combine lpf and hpf for bandpass sweeps

name: Noise Injection
description: Add or increase noise components in a sound. White/pink noise blended with tonal elements creates grit, air, or density.
usefulWhen: A sound feels too pure/clean, needs grit or textural complexity
repair: Filter the noise to control which frequency range it occupies. Bandpass noise (300-2000Hz) for midrange grit. High-pass noise (>4kHz) for air.
strudelHints: Layer s('noise') with the tonal element at low gain
.gain('<0 0.1 0.2 0.1 0>').slow(8) on the noise layer for pulsing texture
.lpf() on noise to control harshness

name: Metallic Infection
description: Replace or blend organic/warm timbres with metallic, ringing, industrial sounds. The sound becomes harder, colder, more mechanical.
usefulWhen: The timbre feels too warm/organic/soft for the concept
repair: Don't apply to all layers — keep at least one warm element for contrast. Pure metallic timbre without warmth becomes fatiguing.
strudelHints: Use s('metal:1 metal:2 metal:3') instead of or layered with standard drum sounds
.room(0.2) on metallic hits for a close, hard sound
Layering: original sound at 50% gain + metallic version at 50%

name: Filter Morph
description: Slowly transform a sound's timbre through continuous filter movement. The filter becomes the primary musical gesture.
usefulWhen: Creating a sense of continuous evolution, revealing and hiding frequency content over time
repair: Use very slow modulation (slow(16) minimum). Faster filter movements become wah-wah effects rather than textural evolution.
strudelHints: Combine lpf and room changes for compound textural shifts

name: Soften Attack
description: Reduce or remove the attack transient from percussive sounds. The sound becomes a texture rather than a hit — more pad-like, less percussive.
usefulWhen: Percussion elements are too prominent or sharp for the desired texture
repair: Combine with increased reverb to further diffuse the sound. The softened attack + long reverb transforms percussion into atmosphere.
strudelHints: .decay(2).gain(0.15).room(0.8) — long decay, low gain, high reverb
Remove the attack layer, keep only the decay/sustain

name: Register Shift
description: Move a sound up or down by one or two octaves. Changes the sound's role in the mix: a bass becomes a lead, a high texture becomes a low drone.
usefulWhen: A sound needs to occupy a different frequency register or play a different musical role
repair: After shifting, adjust filtering and gain. An octave-up sound may need .lpf() to control harshness. An octave-down sound may need .hpf() to avoid subsonic mud.
strudelHints: .fast(0.5) for octave down
.fast(2) for octave up
Use note() with higher/lower octave numbers: note('d1') → note('d2')

name: Frequency Modulation Drift
description: Apply very slow frequency modulation (FM) to a sound, causing its harmonic content to gradually shift. Creates a sense of organic instability.
usefulWhen: A static drone or tone needs organic, evolving movement
repair: Use very low modulation depth and very slow rate. The effect should be subliminal — the listener should sense change without hearing modulation.
strudelHints: Layer two very close frequencies with slight detuning for beating
.lpf() with very slow modulation overlaid on the FM for compound evolution
